newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo share rise spotlights chance of higher rates.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo share rise spotlights chance of higher rates.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market returned from a long holiday weekend in a bullish mood on Tuesday, with the key index climbing to its highest level in four months on Wall Street's advance and investors' bids for blue-chip shares.

Traders said the unexpectedly robust rally had increased expectations of an early end to Japan's ultra-soft monetary policy, capping the dollar's rise against the yen and triggering a sell-off in Japanese government bonds.
The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares soared above the key 20,000 level soon after the opening, the first time it had crossed that barrier since December 19.

The 225-share Nikkei average jumped 666.17 points or 3.41 percent -- its second-largest one-day gain this year -- to end at 20,180.92, the highest closing level since 20,413.46 set on December 17. June Nikkei futures rose 660 points to 20,190.

"Rounds of buying in issues which were far behind the popular blue chips, such as some financials and domestic demand-sensitive shares, in addition to bellwether issues, powered the market higher," said Noboru Yorita, general manager at Tachibana Securities Co Ltd.
Turnover ballooned to 715 million shares, the third-largest volume so far this year. On Friday, 487 million shares changed hands. Japanese markets were closed on Monday for a holiday.
The rally set the dollar drifting down to just below 126.00 yen in late Tokyo against its New York close of around 126.60 yen, and triggered a jump in Japanese long-term interest rates.

Traders said speculation was growing that the stock market's strength would take pressure off Japan to maintain its current ultra-soft monetary policy, as it would benefit the fragile banking and other financial sectors.

"Earlier, the market had felt the BOJ would raise interest rates no earlier than around September, but now some think rates may be raised in July, after the release of the BOJ's key 'tankan' survey," a senior trust bank trader said.

The yield of the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond rose more than 10 basis points to 2.420 percent in late Tokyo. Key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures ended down more than a full point at 124.33.

"Worries over downside risks have diminished recently, and the surge in U.S. stocks lifted the Nikkei 225 more steeply than expected," said Hisao Suzuki, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.

On Monday, the Dow Jones Industrial average closed above 7,200 points for the first time ever on hopes that a balanced federal budget deal would keep the U.S. Federal Reserve from raising interest rates later this month.

A rise in the technology-orientated Nasdaq index in particular inspired foreign investors to seek electricals and high-tech issues in Tokyo such as Hitachi and Fujitsu, which were seen having room to rise, brokers said.
Other Japanese blue-chip shares such as electronics giant Sony Corp and carmaker Toyota Motor Corp also climbed to record highs on Tuesday.
They were helped by the recent weakness of the yen, which makes their products more competitive abroad, brokers said.

Despite the recent gains, some remained sceptical about the possibility of further advances. "Unless there are fresh fundamental factors, shares are unlikely to rally further in the face of prevailing strong caution about the topside," said an official at a second-tier Japanese brokerage. ($1=126 yen)
